questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Center of a Vertical Hyperbola
questions.problem: What is the center of the hyperbola $\frac{(y-1)^{2}}{16}-\frac{(x-5)^{2}}{4}=1?$
questions.worked_solution:
The equation of a vertical hyperbola centered at $(h,k)$ is given by

$$
\frac{(y-k)^{2}}{{a}^{2}}-\frac{(x-h)^{2}}{{b}^{2}}=1.
$$

In this case, we have $h=5$ and $k=1.$

Therefore, the center of the hyperbola is $(5,1).$

questions.problem:
The center of the hyperbola $5{y}^{2}-2{x}^{2}-20y+4x=-8$ is$\,\,($
{{field-1}}$,$
{{field-2}}
$).$
questions.worked_solution:
The equation of a vertical hyperbola centered at $(h,k)$ is given by

$$
\frac{(y-k)^{2}}{{a}^{2}}-\frac{(x-h)^{2}}{{b}^{2}}=1.
$$

To rewrite the equation of the hyperbola in the above form, we need to group $x$ and $y$ terms and complete the squares, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}5{y}^{2}-2{x}^{2}-20y+4x & =-8 \\ 5{y}^{2}-20y-2{x}^{2}+4x & =-8 \\ 5[{y}^{2}-4y]-2[{x}^{2}-2x] & =-8 \\ 5[(y-2)^{2}-4]-2[(x-1)^{2}-1] & =-8 \\ 5(y-2)^{2}-20-2(x-1)^{2}+2 & =-8 \\ 5(y-2)^{2}-2(x-1)^{2} & =-8+20-2 \\ 5(y-2)^{2}-2(x-1)^{2} & =10 \\ \frac{(y-2)^{2}}{2}-\frac{(x-1)^{2}}{5} & =1\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, the center of the hyperbola is $(\,1,2\,).$

questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Center of a Horizontal Hyperbola Given an Equation in Expanded Form
questions.problem:
The center of the hyperbola $4{x}^{2}-{y}^{2}-8x+6y=11$ is$\,\,($
{{field-1}}$,$
{{field-2}}
$).$
questions.worked_solution:
The equation of a horizontal hyperbola centered at $(h,k)$ is given by

$$
\frac{(x-h)^{2}}{{a}^{2}}-\frac{(y-k)^{2}}{{b}^{2}}=1.
$$

To rewrite the given equation in standard form, group the $x$ and $y$ terms and complete the squares:

$$
\begin{aligned}4{x}^{2}-{y}^{2}-8x+6y & =11 \\ 4({x}^{2}-2x)-({y}^{2}-6y) & =11 \\ 4[(x-1)^{2}-1]-[(y-3)^{2}-9] & =11 \\ 4(x-1)^{2}-4-(y-3)^{2}+9 & =11 \\ 4(x-1)^{2}-(y-3)^{2} & =11+4-9 \\ 4(x-1)^{2}-(y-3)^{2} & =6 \\ \frac{(x-1)^{2}}{3/2}-\frac{(y-3)^{2}}{6} & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, the center of the hyperbola is $(\,1,3\,).$

questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Center of a Vertical Hyperbola Given an Equation in Expanded Form
questions.problem:
The center of the hyperbola $-{x}^{2}+16{y}^{2}-32y-8x=16$ is$\,\,($
{{field-1}}$,$
{{field-2}}
$).$
questions.worked_solution:
The equation of a vertical hyperbola centered at $(h,k)$ is given by

$$
\frac{(y-k)^{2}}{{a}^{2}}-\frac{(x-h)^{2}}{{b}^{2}}=1.
$$

To rewrite the equation of the hyperbola in the above form, we need to group $x$ and $y$ terms and complete the squares, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}-{x}^{2}+16{y}^{2}-32y-8x & =16 \\ 16{y}^{2}-32y-{x}^{2}-8x & =16 \\ 16[{y}^{2}-2y]-[{x}^{2}+8x] & =16 \\ 16[(y-1)^{2}-1]-[(x+4)^{2}-16] & =16 \\ 16(y-1)^{2}-16-(x+4)^{2}+16 & =16 \\ 16(y-1)^{2}-(x+4)^{2} & =16 \\ \frac{(y-1)^{2}}{1}-\frac{(x+4)^{2}}{16} & =1 \\ \frac{(y-1)^{2}}{1}-\frac{(x-(-4))^{2}}{16} & =1\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, the center of the hyperbola is $(\,-4,1\,).$
